questions.solution_text:
Base: $18\times10=180$
Triangles on the $18\text{ cm}$ edges: $2\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times18\times13\right)=234$
Triangles on the $10\text{ cm}$ edges: $2\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times10\times15\right)=150$
$SA=180+234+150$
$=564\text{ cm}^{2}$

questions.question_text: A right square pyramid has a surface area of $360\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a base edge of $10\text{ cm}$. Find its perpendicular height.

options.why: Used the slant height $13$ as the perpendicular height without the final Pythagoras step.
Added the squares instead of subtracting when finding the perpendicular height.
Doubled the slant height instead of using Pythagoras with half the base edge.

questions.solution_text:
Base: $10\times10=100$
Triangles: $360-100=260$, so $260=20l$ and $l=13\text{ cm}$
Half the base edge is $5\text{ cm}$.
$h=\sqrt{13^{2}-5^{2}}=\sqrt{144}=12\text{ cm}$
